research_question: Does controlled loss of measured molecules affect a covariate-adjusted ranking diagnostic through the model scores, the independently estimated diagnostic covariates, or their joint change?
model: native scTenifoldKnk 2.0.0 transcriptomeWide heat distance; nc_nNet=10, nc_nComp=3, nc_q=0.9, ma_heatT=10, dr_direction=false
model_input: Exactly the 400 D control cells and fixed gene/target lists in the verified earlier model preparation; integer UMI thinning independently per observed count; no gene reselection
diagnostic_covariate_input: All D control cells outside the 400 model cells; no A/B/C cells. Normalize counts using each cell's sum across the full retained curated gene universe, multiply by 10000 then log1p, and estimate mean expression on model genes. Use the same fixed cells at every q; any zero-library cell causes an explicit failed condition rather than silent selection.
covariate_thinning: Binomial thinning on all retained curated genes, before normalization; distinct deterministic RNG stream from model-input thinning
S0_Cq_interpretation: Frozen scores and frozen external response; only the measured adjustment covariate changes. Tests sensitivity of a diagnostic to covariate estimation, not whether any population confounder has been removed.
Sq_C0_interpretation: Model input changes while diagnostic covariate and response remain fixed; includes genuine information loss.
Sq_Cq_interpretation: Both model and diagnostic covariates change under the same thinning probability but independent cell pools and RNG streams.
score_policy: Distance >=0 finite; larger is higher. EDR uses signed residuals of log10(max(distance,1e-10)) regressed on mean control expression with intercept. Do not take absolute residuals. Record floor counts.
evaluation_scope: One fixed model-feature universe excluding every directly targeted gene in that dataset; same genes for all tasks, thinning conditions and source-ranking comparisons
outcomes: Top50 selection overlap with unthinned baseline
R2 of logscore on mean control expression
same-target minus all-other-target mean B*C identity gain
controls: q=1 native model refit compared with archived scores
q=1 alternative model seeds to measure algorithmic variation
target-invariant control-expression ranking must have zero identity gain
independent empirical A-response ranking is a technical repeatability anchor, not a prediction model or mathematical ceiling
control-vs-control B/C outcomes evaluated against actual target-specific model scores
summary: Report every prespecified condition. Average thinning seeds within target before across-target summaries. Targets share controls; no biological-replicate p-values or population CIs. Sign changes are descriptive; near-zero sign flips alone cannot justify innovation.
success_criterion: Pilot advances only if a diagnostic behavior can be attributed to a specific arm of the factorial design and has material consequences for reproducible response or model comparison beyond q=1 algorithmic variability; it must be distinguished from ordinary information loss. External confirmation and comparison with established diagnostics are still required.
limitations: This is a development feasibility test on previously examined data, not a registered confirmatory experiment.
The upstream curated gene universe was selected using all cells. Fixed-scope effects are conditional on this historical universe; the pipeline is not fully outcome-blind.
Binomial thinning is a randomized computational intervention conditional on observed molecules; it is not a new biological or sequencing experiment.
The B/C response scale uses the existing verified curated X normalization; it is fixed across interventions and is not absolute RNA abundance.
Two K562 studies and one native model mode do not establish generality to foundation models, other cell types or biological replicates.
No expression-associated response is automatically called artifact, and no residualization result is interpreted as causal mediation.
